text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Malaysia is setting up a tribunal to deal with problems and complaints after the Rent Control Act has been abolished, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says.
-- Bus companies have been given until mid-February to improve their bus services in Kuala Lumpur.
-- Anwar tells all parties involved in the investigations into log smuggling activities in eastern Sabah state to stop making accusations and offending statements.
-- The government will in future be more liberal in the issuance of share broking licences to trust agencies, Anwar says.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad directs Sabah state government and Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik to refrain from making anymore statements on the seven million ringgit log smuggling case.
-- Police seizes about 200 kg of marijuana from a fishing boat in northern Penang state, believed to be the largest haul in recent years.
